newsitem.title: BRAZIL: GM eyes 4th Brazil plant, mum on details.
newsitem.headline: GM eyes 4th Brazil plant, mum on details.

text.p: General Motors is "strongly interested" in building a fourth plant in Brazil and is studying the idea, but can offer no details on the possible factory, a spokesman for the U.S. automaker's local unit said.
"GM has strong interest in building a fourth factory, we're studying it, but no decision has been taken," GM do Brasil spokesman Carlos Augusto Souza told Reuters.
But he could not provide details on a possible price tag, location or operations of a new GM plant in Brazil.

Souza's comments came several hours after GM formally inaugurated its latest operation, a $70 million GMC truck plant that began producing this month, and introduced its new president, Frederic Henderson.
He said the firm will make a decision "in the coming months" on whether or not to build a new factory, but he declined to say if a new factory would produce components or vehicles.
GM hopes to take advantage not only of the burgeoning Brazilian market, but of markets in other rapidly growing regional economies.
The firm, which has decided to focus its operations for the Mercosur trade bloc and the rest of South America in Brazil, plans to invest some $4 billion in the country by 2000, he added.

GM do Brasil's exports in 1996 totalled $750 million and the company's goal for this year is $1 billion. Mercosur is comprised of Argentina, Brazil, Paraguay and Uruguay with Chile as an associate member.
